transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Your Name]. What brings you in today? Is there something specific you'd like to talk about?

Hi, Doctor. Well, I mostly came in because I’m just tired all the time. It’s like... by midmorning at work, I'm already done. I’ll just be reviewing some files or walking one of the junior adjusters through a claim—which, honestly, we just hired this new girl, and she’s sweet, but she really doesn't grasp the new appraisal software they forced on us last month. They updated the whole system and didn't even give us a proper training seminar, just this massive PDF manual. I tried printing it out to read on my lunch break, but the printer on our floor has been jamming every single time you try to do double-sided, and maintenance takes forever to come look at it. 

Anyway, sorry, what was I saying? Oh, right. Just doing the basics, like helping her or looking at a few standard claims... by 10:30 in the morning, it feels like my body and my brain are already running completely on empty.
Do you wake up in the morning already feeling tired, or does the fatigue seem to come on during the day?

Well, like I said, it really hits me hard by midmorning at work, where I'm just completely spent after looking at a few files. But... honestly, I wake up feeling pretty drained, too. 

My alarm goes off at 6:00 and I just... I don't know, I just lay there. I used to get up right away and make a full pot of coffee. We had this great old Hamilton Beach coffee maker, the kind with the glass carafe? My sister gave it to me for Christmas like, oh, it must have been ten years ago. She always gives the most practical gifts. Last year she gave me a set of those wool dryer balls. Have you ever used those? They actually do cut down on the drying time, which is nice because our dryer is on its last legs and makes this awful screeching noise if you put too many heavy towels in it at once. The repair guy said it would cost more to fix than to just buy a new one, which is just how everything is nowadays, isn't it? Nobody fixes anything, they just throw it in a landfill. 

But anyway... what were we talking about? Oh, the mornings. Yeah, I wake up already feeling tired, and then by the time I've been at my desk for a couple of hours dealing with those claims, my brain is just totally running on empty again.
Have you noticed any changes in how you feel about the things you used to enjoy, like hobbies or spending time with family and friends?

Well, honestly, I've really pulled back from a lot of things. I used to love painting, and I'd go hiking on the weekends, or volunteer... but lately, I'm just trying to get through the week. It's like I don't have the energy for any of it anymore. Even at work, I've started missing details in audits, and it's taking me way longer to sign off on files. 

Which is a real problem because my supervisor, Gary, he's a stickler for turnaround times. He's been with the company for twenty-five years, and he still uses this ancient label maker for all his physical folders. You can hear it clicking away from three cubicles down. Click, click, click. It drives the new girl absolutely crazy. She actually asked me if we could requisition a digital one for him, but I told her, 'Honey, Gary is not giving up that label maker until he retires.' He’s got this whole system where red tape means urgent, yellow means pending... but he ran out of yellow tape last month and started using this neon green color, and it completely threw off the filing clerks. They were bringing him closed files thinking they were new assignments. It was a whole mess on Tuesday. 

But yeah... what was the question? Oh, hobbies. Yeah, I just don't do much of anything anymore outside of work. I'm just too exhausted.
Have you been feeling down, sad, or hopeless most of the time lately?

Well, yeah, I guess I have. It's... most days I feel like there’s this gray film over everything. Like, even when my husband is being really sweet or we’re all in the kitchen cooking with the family, I'm just going through the motions. I don't really feel that spark or enjoyment I used to. 

We were making lasagna last Sunday, actually. My mother's recipe. She always insisted on using half ground beef and half Italian sausage, which really does make a difference in the flavor. But you have to get the mild sausage, not the spicy, or it totally overpowers the ricotta. We used to get the sausage from this little deli down on 4th Street, but they closed during the pandemic and never reopened. It's a shame, they had the best cured meats. Now they're turning the building into another one of those boutique fitness places. I think it's a Pilates studio? My neighbor Sarah goes to one of those, and she says it's great for your core, but honestly, who wants to pay thirty dollars a class just to stretch on a fancy machine? 

Sorry, I'm wandering again, aren't I? But yes, to answer your question, I just feel kind of down and disconnected most of the time, even when good things are happening around me.
Have you lost interest in activities you used to enjoy, like painting or hiking?

Well, yes, I think we just talked about that a minute ago, but yeah, I really have. I just don't have the energy for the painting or the hiking anymore. I haven't touched my canvases in months. 

Actually, the last thing I tried to paint was a landscape from a photo I took at Mount Rainier. We went there for our anniversary a couple of years ago. It was so beautiful, but the traffic getting into the park was an absolute nightmare. We sat in a line of cars for over an hour just to get through the toll booth. And the guy in front of us had this bumper sticker that said 'My other ride is a UFO,' which I thought was kind of funny at first, but after staring at it for an hour, it just got annoying. We finally got in and did the Skyline Trail, which is where I took the photo. It was gorgeous, but my husband wore these new hiking boots he hadn't broken in yet, and he got the worst blisters. I told him he needed to wear them around the house first, but you know how men are, they never listen. He ended up having to buy these expensive moleskin pads at the visitor center... 

But anyway, yeah, I haven't painted that picture or any other picture in a long time. I just don't care to do it right now.
How long have you been feeling this way? Have these feelings of fatigue, sadness, and loss of interest been going on for at least two weeks, or longer?

Oh, two weeks? No, no, it's been way longer than that. I'd say it's been about... well, probably three years and three months now. Yeah, that sounds right. It started right around the time I was moved into this new role at work. They gave me a lot more responsibility, having me mentor the new adjusters and oversee the rollout of our new workflow systems. 

Which, let me tell you, those new systems were a complete disaster when they first launched. The IT department swore up and down that the transition would be seamless, but the first week, nobody could access the old claim files. It was a nightmare. I had adjusters calling me in a panic because they had clients on the phone asking about their settlements, and we couldn't even pull up the policy numbers. And the interface! They changed all the color coding. We used to have blue for auto claims and green for property, but they switched it to this weird pastel palette that you can barely read on the monitors. I actually had to go out and buy a pair of blue-light glasses just to stare at the screen all day. I found a nice pair at Costco, actually, in a tortoiseshell frame. They came in a two-pack, so I gave the extra pair to my husband, but he keeps leaving them in his truck where they get all smudged up...

But anyway, what was I saying? Oh, right, the timeline. Yeah, it's been over three years since I started feeling this way, ever since that promotion.
Have you been feeling like you're not good enough, or that you're letting people down at work or at home?

Well, no, not really. I mean, I don't feel like I'm letting anyone down or that I'm not good enough. I just... I do my job, and I take care of the house, even if I'm just going through the motions. I still get it all done. 

Like yesterday, I managed to get all the laundry washed, dried, and folded. Which is a miracle in itself because our dryer has been making this awful squeaking noise for the last month. It sounds like there's a family of mice living in the drum. My husband said he was going to look at it, but you know, he gets distracted. He started watching this documentary series on the History Channel about ancient Roman engineering, and suddenly he's an expert on aqueducts. He spent two hours on Sunday explaining to me how they mixed volcanic ash into their concrete to make it set underwater. Which, I mean, is fascinating, I guess, if you're into that sort of thing. But it doesn't get the dryer fixed, does it? I ended up having to call the repair guy we used when the dishwasher broke last Thanksgiving. Remember that? Oh wait, you wouldn't know. The heating element went out right in the middle of the wash cycle, and all my good china came out covered in this greasy film. I had to hand wash everything while the turkey was resting...

Anyway, what were we talking about? Oh, feeling like I'm not good enough. No, I don't really have those kinds of thoughts. I just feel tired and empty, but I know I'm still doing what I'm supposed to do.
Have you noticed any changes in your weight recently, like losing or gaining a significant amount without trying?

Weight? No, my weight has been pretty much exactly the same. I know for sure because I just had to buy some new slacks for work last weekend. Our office decided to enforce a strict business casual dress code again, which is honestly ridiculous because we're on a hybrid schedule now and half the time nobody even sees us in person anyway. 

But I went down to Kohl's to get a couple of pairs of basic black pants. I usually get the ones with the little bit of stretch in the waistband, but they completely rearranged the women's department. It took me twenty minutes just to find the misses section, and when I finally did, this woman was blocking the entire aisle with her shopping cart, just staring at her phone. I swear, people have zero spatial awareness these days. She was watching some video on full volume—sounded like a recipe for a casserole or something with a lot of cheese. I had to squeeze past the clearance rack just to get around her, and I ended up knocking a bunch of those silk scarves onto the floor. I tried to pick them up, but the hangers were all tangled together... 

But, um, what was I saying? Oh, right, my weight. Yeah, no, I bought the exact same size twelve I've been wearing for the last five years and they fit just like always. So no, I haven't noticed any changes there.
Have you had trouble focusing on tasks, making decisions, or thinking clearly lately?

Focusing? Yeah, actually, that's... that's been getting harder. At work, I've started missing details in my audits, which is really not like me. And it's taking me so much longer to sign off on files. I just sit there staring at the screen, reading the same paragraph over and over. 

Which is exactly what happened on Tuesday with this one claim from a guy who hit a deer in his Subaru. I swear, the police report was the most poorly written document I've ever seen. The officer kept referring to the deer as the "suspect," which I guess was supposed to be funny, but it just made it confusing. And the photos the guy submitted of the damage... he must have taken them with a potato. They were so blurry, I couldn't tell if the bumper was cracked or if it was just a shadow from the pine tree in his driveway. Speaking of pine trees, we have this massive one in our front yard that's been dropping needles everywhere. My husband was supposed to rake them up last weekend, but remember I told you about that Roman engineering documentary? Yeah, he was still watching that. He even bought a book about it on Amazon. It arrived yesterday, and the delivery driver left it right on the edge of the porch where it could have gotten soaked if it rained. Luckily, it didn't, but still...

Wait, what was the question? Oh, right, making decisions and focusing. Yeah, it's bad at work, and even outside of work, I've just completely pulled back from everything. I used to love painting, and hiking, and I volunteered at the animal shelter on Saturdays, but now... I just can't. I'm just trying to get through the week, you know? It just takes everything I have to just get to Friday.
Have you noticed that your ability to think clearly, concentrate, or make decisions has gotten worse lately?

Didn't you just ask me that? Or maybe I'm losing my mind. Like I just said, it's mainly just the audits at work taking me forever. I don't think it's gotten any worse than what I was just telling you. 

Though my brain does feel a bit scrambled sometimes, kind of like how they have the traffic patterns set up on Interstate 84 right now. Have you driven through there lately? It is an absolute disaster. They've got those heavy concrete barriers pushing everyone into one lane, and nobody knows how to zipper merge. Yesterday, this woman in a giant white SUV—one of those Escalades that's way too big for just one person—she completely refused to let anyone in. She was literally putting on mascara in the rearview mirror while riding the bumper of the semi-truck in front of her. I was terrified she was going to rear-end him and cause a massive pileup. And of course, I was stuck right behind her, just staring at her license plate. It was from Florida. Why are there so many Florida plates up here this time of year? Usually the snowbirds go south for the winter, not the other way around. My aunt Carol lives in Boca Raton, and she says the traffic down there is just as bad, especially near the Publix... 

Um... wait, what were we talking about? Oh, right, my concentration. Yeah, no, I think I already answered that. I haven't noticed anything else besides the work stuff I just mentioned.
Over the past few weeks, have you noticed that it's been harder for you to make decisions or focus on tasks, even ones that used to feel simple?

I feel like we're going in circles here. I really don't think it's changed from what I just told you a minute ago. It's just the work audits. The decisions and the focusing... it's just what I said. 

Although, speaking of decisions, I did have to make a choice about my lunch today, which was surprisingly difficult. Our office cafeteria was closed because of some plumbing issue—apparently a pipe burst in the kitchen and flooded the whole prep area. So I had to go down the street to this deli I usually avoid. They have this sandwich, the "Turkey Gobbler" or something, with cranberry sauce and stuffing on it. It sounds good in theory, but the bread they use is always so dry. It's like eating a sponge. My coworker, Brenda, she swears by their egg salad, but I can't do egg salad from a place I don't trust. You just never know how long it's been sitting out. Plus, Brenda has an iron stomach. She ate gas station sushi once on a road trip to Albany and didn't even get a stomachache. I would have been in the hospital for a week. 

Anyway... sorry, what did you ask me? Was it about the audits again? Because yeah, no, nothing's changed with my focus since you asked the first time.
Have you noticed that your movements or speech have slowed down, or that you feel more restless or agitated lately?

Slowed down? Or restless? No, I don't think so. I haven't noticed anything like that. I mean, I'm just sitting at my desk most of the day anyway. 

Though my desk chair is incredibly uncomfortable, which might make anyone restless. It's one of those cheap mesh ones they bought in bulk five years ago. The lumbar support hits me right in the wrong spot, right where I pulled a muscle last summer trying to lift a bag of mulch. I was gardening, trying to fix up the flower beds before my mother-in-law came to visit. She always makes these little passive-aggressive comments about my hydrangeas. Like, "Oh, yours are so... quaint. Mine are already blooming beautifully." She uses this special fertilizer she orders from some catalog, and she won't tell me what it is. It's like a state secret. She keeps the bag hidden in her garage behind the snowblower. My husband says I shouldn't let it bother me, but it's just the principle of the thing, you know? Why be so secretive about fertilizer? 

Anyway, sorry, what were we talking about? Oh, right, moving slow or being restless. No, I don't think I've had any issues with that.
Have you found it difficult to think clearly or concentrate on tasks, even ones you used to handle easily?

Are you... didn't we just do this? I feel like I'm taking a pop quiz where every question is the same. No, like I keep saying, it's just the audits taking longer. My thinking is the same as it was the last three times you asked. 

Though, thinking clearly... you know what makes it impossible to think clearly? The lighting in our office. They switched out all the bulbs last month to these ultra-bright LEDs to "save energy" or whatever. It's like working inside a refrigerator. It gives me this awful glare on my dual monitors. I tried asking IT if they could get me one of those anti-glare screens, but you know how IT is. You submit a ticket, and it goes into a black hole. The guy who usually helps me, Kevin, he's great, but he transferred to the regional office in Omaha. Which is crazy to me, because who wants to move to Omaha? He said housing is cheaper, but is it worth the winters? My cousin moved to Nebraska once, and she said the wind just howls across the plains. There's nothing to stop it. She lasted two years before she moved back to the East Coast. 

Wait... what was I saying? Oh, right, the concentration thing. Yeah, no, nothing new to report there. Just the work stuff I already mentioned.
Have you noticed a significant loss of energy or feel fatigued, even after resting or sleeping?

Well, yeah, actually, that's really why I came in. I'm just tired all the time. By midmorning at work, honestly, after just reviewing some files or walking one of the junior adjusters through a claim, it feels like my body and my brain are already completely running on empty. 

Speaking of the junior adjusters, they just hired this new kid, Tyler. He's fresh out of college, and he always brings in these massive iced coffees. You know, the kind in the plastic cups that sweat condensation everywhere? He sets it right on top of the paper files. It drives me crazy. I told him he needs to get a coaster, so he brought in this novelty one shaped like a tiny vinyl record. Which is funny, because vinyl is making this huge comeback right now. My husband kept all his old records from the eighties down in our basement, and they just smell like mildew at this point. I keep telling him we should sell them at a garage sale or put them on eBay, but he's convinced they're some kind of retirement investment. Like, who is going to pay top dollar for a scratched-up Def Leppard album? It makes no sense. We could use the space for a chest freezer instead, especially with meat prices being what they are. 

But anyway... what were you asking? Oh, about being tired. Yeah, like I said, by midmorning I just have no energy left at all.
Have you ever experienced a period of time before this one where you felt similarly down, fatigued, or lost interest in things for several weeks or more?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I've had stressful times, sure, but nothing like this where it just drags on and on. I've always been pretty steady, you know? 

Like when the company merged back in 2018, that was stressful, but I got through it fine. Though the merger was a complete disaster in other ways. They brought in all new management from the acquiring company, and they had no idea how our state's insurance regulations worked. This one guy, Bradley, he kept trying to implement these "streamlined" procedures that were actually illegal under state law. I had to pull out the actual statute book and highlight it for him. And he still argued with me! He had this really annoying habit of clicking his pen while he talked. Click, click, click. It drove me up the wall. It was one of those expensive metal pens, too, not a cheap plastic one. My daughter got me a really nice pen for Mother's Day once, but it ran out of ink and I could never find the right refills for it at the office supply store. They always had every brand except the one I needed. It's like they do it on purpose, right? Just to make you buy a whole new pen. 

But, uh, no. To answer your question, I haven't ever felt like this before. This is definitely new for me.
Have you ever had a period lasting two weeks or more when you felt down, lost interest in things, or had little energy, before this current one started?

Are you... didn't you just ask me that? Like, literally the exact same question just a minute ago? I feel like we're going in circles here. 

No, like I just said, I've never had a period like this before. I've always been the steady one. Even when things get chaotic, I just put my head down and work. 

Like with my sister's wedding back in the nineties. Oh my gosh, what a nightmare that was. The caterer backed out two weeks before the date, and my mother was having an absolute meltdown. She was calling everyone in the tri-state area trying to find someone who could do a sit-down dinner for two hundred people on a Saturday in June. It was impossible. We ended up having to go with this buffet place that mostly did corporate lunches, and the food was just... well, it was edible, but barely. The chicken was so dry you needed a gallon of water just to swallow it. And don't even get me started on the DJ. He played the Macarena three times. Three times! Who wants to do the Macarena in a heavy satin bridesmaid dress? I was sweating through the fabric, and the color was this awful seafoam green that washes out my complexion anyway. I still have the dress in a garment bag in the attic. I don't know why I keep it. Maybe I thought my daughter would want to wear it for Halloween or something, but she's more into those scary costumes with the fake blood. 

Anyway... yeah. I already answered this. No, I haven't felt this way before. It's just been recently.
Before this current period, have you ever had an episode where you felt down or lost interest in things for at least two weeks?

Okay, is this a test? Are you testing my memory or something? Because you literally just asked me that. Twice now. I feel like I'm taking crazy pills here. 

No. For the third time, no. I have never felt like this before. It's just this one long stretch that I'm in right now. I don't know how else to say it. 

I mean, if you want to talk about memory tests, my mother-in-law had to take one of those when she started getting forgetful. They made her draw a clock, which is so outdated if you think about it. Who even looks at analog clocks anymore? My husband bought one of those smart displays for the kitchen counter, and it just shows the time in big digital numbers, plus the weather. It's supposed to show our family photos as a screensaver, but he set it up wrong, so it just cycles through the stock photos that came with the device. There's this one picture of a golden retriever running through a field of lavender that pops up every five minutes. We don't even own a dog. We had a cat once, Mr. Whiskers, but he ruined the upholstery on my favorite armchair. It was this beautiful floral print wingback chair I found at an antique store in Vermont. We took a road trip up there for the fall foliage, and the leaves were just... spectacular. 

But seriously, doctor. I've already answered this. No previous episodes. Just this current one. Can we please move on to the next question?
Before this current period, have you ever had an episode where you felt down or lost interest in things for at least two weeks?

Are you serious right now? Are you reading from a broken script or something? Because this is the fourth time—the *fourth* time—you've asked me the exact same thing. I'm starting to wonder if I'm the one who should be asking the questions here. 

I don't... I just don't know what you want me to say that I haven't already said. No. The answer is still no. Never before this. Just now. Just this one time that's been going on forever. 

It's like dealing with customer service at the cable company. You call them up because the internet keeps dropping out, and every time they transfer you to a new person, you have to explain the whole problem all over again. And they always ask, "Have you tried unplugging the router?" Yes, Kevin, I've unplugged the router. I unplugged it, I waited thirty seconds, I plugged it back in, and the little light is still blinking orange instead of green. It's supposed to be a solid green light. I know this because the installation guy, he was this young kid, maybe twenty, he showed me specifically. He had these huge gauge earrings, you know, the ones that stretch out your earlobes? I always wonder what happens to those when they get older. Do the holes just stay there, or do they shrink back? I saw a documentary once about indigenous tribes in the Amazon who do that, but it has a cultural significance for them. I doubt the kid installing my Wi-Fi was doing it for cultural reasons. Probably just trying to annoy his parents. 

Look, I'm sorry if I'm getting snappy, but I just... I really need you to listen to me. No previous times like this. Okay? Can we please, please talk about something else?

target_item.name: Fatigue
target_item.manifestation: I came in because I’m tired all the time—by midmorning at work, after just reviewing files or walking a junior adjuster through a claim, it feels like my body and my brain are already running on empty.

patient.answer:

target_item.reason: The doctor is repeatedly asking about a history of Major Depressive Episodes prior to the current persistent depression (past MDEs). My symptom profile does not include information about past episodes, and I have already answered this question multiple times in the dialogue.

patient.answer:
Are you serious right now? Are you reading from a broken script or something? Because this is the fourth time—the *fourth* time—you've asked me the exact same thing. I'm starting to wonder if I'm the one who should be asking the questions here. 

I don't... I just don't know what you want me to say that I haven't already said. No. The answer is still no. Never before this. Just now. Just this one time that's been going on forever. 

It's like dealing with customer service at the cable company. You call them up because the internet keeps dropping out, and every time they transfer you to a new person, you have to explain the whole problem all over again. And they always ask, "Have you tried unplugging the router?" Yes, Kevin, I've unplugged the router. I unplugged it, I waited thirty seconds, I plugged it back in, and the little light is still blinking orange instead of green. It's supposed to be a solid green light. I know this because the installation guy, he was this young kid, maybe twenty, he showed me specifically. He had these huge gauge earrings, you know, the ones that stretch out your earlobes? I always wonder what happens to those when they get older. Do the holes just stay there, or do they shrink back? I saw a documentary once about indigenous tribes in the Amazon who do that, but it has a cultural significance for them. I doubt the kid installing my Wi-Fi was doing it for cultural reasons. Probably just trying to annoy his parents. 

Look, I'm sorry if I'm getting snappy, but I just... I really need you to listen to me. No previous times like this. Okay? Can we please, please talk about something else?
